guarantees.claim: data_in_mask_o is continuously assigned as the bit-swapped concatenation {data_in_mask[1], data_in_mask[0], data_in_mask[3], data_in_mask[2]}.

The u_aes_sub_bytes instance connects all ports as coded, driving sub_bytes_out, sb_out_mask, sub_bytes_err, and sub_bytes_out_req according to the aes_sub_bytes module implementation given the listed inputs.

assumptions.claim: External logic must adhere to the handshake protocol of aes_sub_bytes: sub_bytes_en must be asserted appropriately to initiate a computation, and sub_bytes_out_ack must acknowledge when output is accepted.
assumptions.cond: when sub_bytes is in use (en_i transitions or out_req_o asserted)
assumptions.risk: Violating handshake may cause the sub_bytes module to stall, produce incorrect outputs, or miss data acceptance, leading to data corruption or loss of synchronization.

assumptions.claim: Inputs sb_in_mask, prd_sub_bytes_q, and state_q[0] must be valid and correctly masked/prd-conditioned as expected by the aes_sub_bytes implementation to ensure proper error detection and security.
assumptions.risk: If masks or PRD are invalid, the sub_bytes module may fail to detect faults or may leak sensitive information through outputs (sub_bytes_out, sb_out_mask, sub_bytes_err).
